'''Niels Erik Nørlund''' {{post-nominals|post-noms=[[Foreign Member of the Royal Society|ForMemRS]]}}<ref name="frs">{{Cite journal | last1 = Bang | first1 = Thøger| doi = 10.1098/rsbm.1983.0017 | doi-access = free| title = Niels Erik Norlund. 26 October 1885-4 July 1981 | journal = [[Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society]] | volume = 29 | pages = 481–493 | year = 1983 | jstor = 769810| s2cid = 73395843}}</ref> (26 October 1885, in [[Slagelse]] &ndash; 4 July 1981, in [[Copenhagen]]) was a [[Denmark|Danish]] [[mathematician]].<ref name="mactutor">{{MacTutor|id=Norlund}}</ref><ref name="mathgene">{{MathGenealogy|id=93550}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Bang | first1 = Thøger G. | doi = 10.1007/BF02392293 | title = Niels Erik Nørlund in memoriam | journal = Acta Mathematica | volume = 161 | pages = 11–22 | year = 1988 | doi-access = free }}</ref>

His book ''Vorlesungen über Differenzenrechnung'' (1924, reprinted 1954) was the first book on [[complex analysis|complex function]] solutions of [[difference equation]]s. His doctoral students include [[Georg Rasch]].

The [[Norlund Alps]] and [[Norlund Land]] in [[Greenland]] were named after him.<ref name="cat">{{cite web | title = Catalogue of place names in northern East Greenland | publisher = Geological Survey of Denmark | url = https://data.geus.dk/geusmap/?mapname=stednavnedb#baslay=baseMapGl&optlay=&extent=549832.8357720698,8582739.868248867,622444.3190166993,8680765.370629115&layers=grl_geus_north_east_higgins_map,grl_ne_higgins_placenames,grl_ne_placenames&filter_1=txt_search.part%3D%26placename%3D&filter_2=txt_search.part%3D%26placename%3D | access-date = 26 September 2019}}</ref>

He was also the brother of [[Margrethe Bohr|Margrethe Nørlund Bohr]] and brother-in-law of Nobel Prize winning physicist [[Niels Bohr]].
